title: A dependency injection container
description:
Write a small DI container that builds objects through their constructors with reflection:

```csharp
public class Container
{
    public void AddSingleton<TService, TImpl>() where TImpl : TService
    public void AddTransient<TService, TImpl>() where TImpl : TService
    public void AddInstance<TService>(TService instance) where TService : notnull
    public T Resolve<T>()
}
```

- `Resolve<T>` looks up the registration for `T`. A **singleton** is created on first use and then reused; a **transient** is created on every resolve; an **instance** is always that object.
- To create an implementation, use its public constructor with the **most parameters**, and resolve each parameter's type from the container (recursively).
- Registering the same service type again replaces the earlier registration.
- Errors (`InvalidOperationException`):
  - `no registration for <TypeName>` when a type (or one of the parameters needed on the way) is not registered;
  - `circular dependency: A -> B -> A` when building a type needs itself, listing the chain of type names.

The sample services (`IClock`, `FixedClock`, `IGreeter`, `Greeter`, `Ping`, `Pong`...) are in the project already.
hints: Keep a list of the types being built right now. If the type you are asked for is already in it, you have found a cycle, and the list (plus the type) is the chain to report.
`impl.GetConstructors()` lists the public constructors; `ctor.GetParameters()` gives their parameter types, and `ctor.Invoke(args)` creates the object.
